subject: management-of-business
title: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart
objectives: Read the maximum stock level, reorder level and buffer stock off the sawtooth stock chart
Calculate the reorder level as buffer stock plus lead-time usage
Explain why stock bottoms out at the buffer, never below it, just as the delivery lands

definitions.meaning: The highest level stock is allowed to reach: here 1,000 units, the level stock jumps back to when a delivery lands.
The stock level at which a new order must be placed: here 500 units, set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage.
The safety floor stock should never fall below, held against late deliveries or unexpected demand: here 250 units.
The time between placing an order and the delivery arriving: here 2 days, during which stock keeps falling.
The steady rate at which stock is used or sold: here 125 units a day, which makes the stock line fall in a straight slope.
The stock chart named for its repeating zigzag shape: stock falls at the usage rate, the delivery jumps it back to maximum, and the tooth repeats. Also called a stock chart.

mechanismSteps: Three levels govern the chart: maximum, reorder, buffer - stock starts full at the maximum stock level of 1,000 units, with the reorder level at 500 units and the buffer stock at 250 units (s1).
Stock falls steadily - crossing the reorder level fires the order: at a usage rate of 125 units a day the falling line reaches 500 units on day 4 and the order is placed (s2).

Through the lead time to the buffer - then the delivery jumps stock back up: stock keeps falling for the 2-day lead time to the buffer of 250 units, and on day 6 the delivery jumps it back to 1,000 units (s3).
The sawtooth repeats: fall, reorder, wait, delivery, jump - the second cycle crosses the reorder level on day 10 to fire the next order (s4).
workedExample: Work through one full cycle for the stocked item. Step 1 (s1): usage is 125 units a day and stock starts at the maximum of 1,000 units. Step 2 (s2): stock falls from 1,000 to 500 in 4 days, because 500 units at 125 units a day takes 4 days, so the order fires on day 4. Step 3 (s3): lead-time usage is 2 x 125 = 250 units, and the reorder level = buffer 250 + lead-time usage 250 = 500 units, which checks against the chart. Step 4 (s3): through the lead time stock falls the remaining 250 units, so stock bottoms at 250 on day 6 as the delivery lands and jumps it back to 1,000 units.

trap.misconception: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away.
trap.explanation: The slip: Buffer stock looks like spare stock sitting idle, and ordering looks like something you do when you have run out - so reordering earlier, while hundreds of units remain, feels wasteful. The fix: Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands. In class, replay scene 3: freeze at the lowest point of the tooth and ask what the stock level is and what arrives at that exact moment - the buffer of 250 units, and the delivery.
